claims.claim: Moliço is gathered on shallow grounds of the ria
Gaining ground upwind is done close-hauled, by tacking
Farmers use moliço to fertilise sandy soil

lines.en: Cast off, Zé. The moliço grows up on the shallow grounds, and the wind comes from there. We go close-hauled and tack. The farmers need it to feed their sandy soil.
lines.pt: Larga, Zé. O moliço está nas praias de moliço, lá para cima, e o vento vem de lá. Vamos à bolina, a virar de bordo. Os lavradores precisam dele para a areia.

claims.claim: Going upwind means sailing close-hauled and tacking from side to side
Moliço fertilises the sandy farmland

lines.en: Sheet in, boy. You don't go straight into the wind: close-hauled, then tack, side to side. The farmers are waiting for the moliço. Their sandy land needs it.
lines.pt: Caça a vela, rapaz. Contra o vento não se vai a direito: bolina e virar de bordo, de um lado para o outro. Os lavradores esperam pelo moliço. A terra arenosa precisa dele.

claims.claim: Low sides let full rakes of moliço be pulled aboard easily
The moliceiro has a flat bottom for shallow water
The boat is about 15 m long with 5 tonnes capacity
The hull is built of pine

lines.en: Why such low sides? So a full rake comes aboard easily, Zé. Flat bottom for shallow water. Fifteen metres of pine, and she carries five tonnes when full.
lines.pt: Porquê tão baixo de borda? Para o ancinho cheio entrar sem custo, Zé. Fundo chato para a pouca água. Quinze metros de pinho, e leva cinco toneladas quando vai cheio.

claims.claim: The pine hull is coated in black pitch to aid caulking and protect the wood
Sarrim is spread over the pitch so crews do not slip

lines.en: That black is pitch, Zé, for caulking and to keep water off the wood. On top, sarrim, so you don't slip. You fell once already. Enough.
lines.pt: Esse negro é breu, Zé, para calafetar e guardar a madeira da água. Por cima, o sarrim, para não escorregares. Já caíste uma vez. Chega.

claims.claim: Moliço gathering was a main source of employment for regional families
As more people worked in the trade, more boats were built
A broad white sail moves the boat

lines.en: Many families live from moliço, Zé. More people in the trade, more boats on the ria. And that broad white sail is what moves us. Keep it full.
lines.pt: Muitas famílias vivem do moliço, Zé. Mais gente no ofício, mais barcos na ria. E essa vela larga e branca é que nos leva. Mantém-na cheia.

claims.claim: As more people worked in the trade, more boats were built and sailed
The moliceiros worked across the whole lagoon

lines.en: So many moliceiros, Ti Manuel! I know: the more people in the trade, the more boats get built. And they work across the whole ria.
lines.pt: Tantos moliceiros, Ti Manuel! Já sei: quanto mais gente no ofício, mais barcos se fazem. E andam por toda a ria.

claims.claim: Moliço gathering was first done by farmers, then became an independent profession supplying farmers

lines.en: Look at them all! First it was the farmers who gathered the moliço. Now some live only from this and sell it to the farmers, right?
lines.pt: Olhe aqueles todos! Primeiro eram os lavradores a apanhar o moliço. Agora há quem viva só disto e o venda aos lavradores, não é?

lines.en: Ease the sail and push!
lines.pt: Folga a vela e empurra!

lines.en: Ease off! Push us free, Zé!
lines.pt: Folga! Empurra para fora, Zé!

claims.claim: Moliço is harvested in the shallow areas of the ria
The moliceiro has a flat bottom for shallow water
A wide, shallow rudder was needed to steer in the shallow moliço grounds

lines.en: Moliço likes the lowest water. That's why the boat is flat and the rudder wide and shallow. You learn the ria's bottom like this.
lines.pt: O moliço gosta da água mais baixa. Por isso o barco é chato e o leme largo e raso. O fundo da ria aprende-se assim.

claims.claim: A wide, shallow rudder was needed to steer in shallow waters
The flat bottom suits shallow water

lines.en: In shallow water, only a wide, shallow rudder steers. Flat bottom, little water. The rest, Zé, you learn by running aground.
lines.pt: Nas águas baixas, só um leme largo e raso governa. Fundo chato, pouca água. O resto, Zé, aprende-se a encalhar.

claims.claim: The moliceiro supplies moliço to farmers
Moliço serves as fertiliser for farmland

lines.en: Boat full. This goes to the farmers, to fertilise the sand. My back aches, as always. But the fields are waiting for us. You've earned your place, Zé.
lines.pt: Barco cheio. Isto vai para os lavradores, para estrumar a areia. Doem-me as costas, como sempre. Mas os campos esperam por nós. Ganhaste o teu lugar, Zé.

claims.claim: The moliceiro gathers moliço and supplies it to farmers
Moliço gathering was a main source of employment for regional families

lines.en: The farmers are waiting. We gather, they fertilise. Many families live from this, Zé. It isn't pretty, it's needed. Tomorrow you come back with me.
lines.pt: Os lavradores estão à espera. Nós apanhamos, eles estrumam. Muitas famílias vivem disto, Zé. Não é bonito, é preciso. Amanhã voltas comigo.

claims.claim: Each moliceiro has four panels, two at the bow and two at the stern
Each panel has a drawing and a caption, and no two panels repeat
The panels use pure primary colours: yellow, green, blue, red, white and black
No moliceiro is considered finished until decorated

lines.en: Look at the panels, Ti Manuel! Two at the bow, two at the stern, each with a drawing and caption. Yellow, green, blue, red, white and black, pure colours. And no two alike. A boat isn't finished without its painting, is it?
lines.pt: Olhe os painéis, Ti Manuel! Dois à proa, dois à popa, cada um com desenho e legenda. Amarelo, verde, azul, vermelho, branco e preto, cores puras. E nenhum é igual a outro. Um barco sem pintura não está acabado, pois não?

claims.claim: Painters usually draw from their own imagination with little input from the owner
The panels have vivid colour, bold outlines and humorous captions
The caption is painted on a white or pink band below the frieze
Panel themes may be religious, humorous or satirical

lines.en: This panel is funny! The painter invents the drawing from his own head, hardly asking the owner. Vivid colours, bold outlines, and the caption on a white or pink band below. There are panels with saints and others poking fun.
lines.pt: Este painel tem graça! O pintor inventa o desenho da cabeça dele, quase sem perguntar ao dono. Cores vivas, contornos fortes, e a legenda numa faixa branca ou cor-de-rosa por baixo. Há painéis de santos e outros a fazer troça.

lines.en: That's it.
lines.pt: Isso.

lines.en: Just like that.
lines.pt: Assim mesmo.

lines.en: Not bad.
lines.pt: Não está mal.

lines.en: Well done, lad.
lines.pt: Bem feito, rapaz.

lines.en: Yes! We did it!
lines.pt: Boa! Conseguimos!

lines.en: Look, it worked!
lines.pt: Olha, resultou!

lines.en: That was great!
lines.pt: Isso foi fixe!

lines.en: That's the way!
lines.pt: Assim é que é!

claims.claim: Moliço is gathered from the lagoon bed.
Moliço is used to fertilize the sandy farmland beside the ria.

lines.en: Moliço comes off the lagoon bed. It goes to the farmers to feed their sandy fields. Without it, sand gives nothing.
lines.pt: O moliço vem do fundo da ria. Vai para os lavradores, para adubar as terras de areia. Sem ele, a areia não dá nada.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: The moliceiro has a flat bottom for the shallow lagoon waters.
Its low sides let rakes full of moliço be pulled aboard easily.

lines.en: Flat bottom, for shallow water. Low sides, so you can haul a full rake aboard without breaking your back.
lines.pt: Fundo chato, para a água baixa. Borda baixa, para puxar o ancinho cheio para dentro sem partir as costas.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: A moliceiro has four painted panels, two at the bow and two at the stern.
It is famed as the most beautiful boat of the Ria.
No moliceiro is considered finished until it is decorated.

lines.en: Four painted panels, two at the bow and two at the stern! They say it's the most beautiful boat on the Ria, and it isn't finished until it's painted.
lines.pt: Quatro painéis pintados, dois à proa e dois à ré! Dizem que é o barco mais bonito da Ria, e que sem pintura nem está acabado.
lines.speaker: k2

claims.claim: Moliço gathering was first done by farmers.
It grew into an independent profession, the moliceiro, who supplies moliço to farmers.

lines.en: Farmers used to gather the moliço themselves. Then it became a trade of its own. The moliceiro gathers, the farmer buys. That's how I live.
lines.pt: Antes eram os próprios lavradores a apanhar o moliço. Depois passou a ofício à parte. O moliceiro apanha, o lavrador compra. Assim vivo eu.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: Painters choose panel themes such as religion, profession or love, usually from their own imagination.
Each drawing has a caption painted on a white or pink band.

lines.en: The painter picks the drawing from his own head: saints, trades, sweethearts... And underneath he paints a caption on a white or pink band.
lines.pt: O pintor é que escolhe o desenho, da cabeça dele: santos, ofícios, amores... E por baixo pinta uma legenda numa faixa branca ou cor-de-rosa.
lines.speaker: k2

claims.claim: Moliceiros are built of pine by traditional shipwrights.
Masters use the pau-de-pontos, a handmade wooden rod used as a ruler that only experienced builders can interpret.

lines.en: Pine boat, made by a master. He measures it all with the pau-de-pontos. A plain stick. Only someone with long years at the trade can read it.
lines.pt: Barco de pinho, feito por mestre. Mede tudo com o pau-de-pontos. Pau simples. Só quem tem muitos anos de ofício o sabe ler.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: Moliço was harvested in shallow areas of the ria.
In the shallow moliço grounds a wide, shallow rudder was needed to steer effectively.

lines.en: On the moliço grounds the water's shallow. That's why the rudder is wide and shallow. A deep rudder would be no use here.
lines.pt: Nas praias de moliço a água é baixa. Por isso o leme é largo e raso. Leme fundo aqui não servia de nada.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: Moliço is a group of 21 aquatic plants growing on the submerged bed of the Ria de Aveiro.

lines.en: I thought moliço was just one weed! Turns out it's twenty-one plants, all growing on the bed of the Ria de Aveiro.
lines.pt: Pensava que o moliço era uma erva só! Afinal são vinte e uma plantas, todas a crescer no fundo da Ria de Aveiro.
lines.speaker: k2
